question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $Y?$

I. $Y∧(¬X∨Y)$

II. $(Y∨¬X)∧¬X$

III. $(¬X∨Y)∧Y$
question.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
Y∧(Y∨¬X)≡Y.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y∧(¬X∨Y) & ≡Y∧(Y∨¬X) \\  & ≡Y.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is *not* logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(Y∨¬X)∧¬X & ≡¬X∧(¬X∨Y) \\  & ≡¬X≢Y.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬X∨Y)∧Y & ≡Y∧(Y∨¬X) \\  & ≡Y.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
